topics.label: Introduction and overview of the hallmarks of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the lecture's learning objectives and frames the conceptual framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and oncogenic signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how mutations in signaling cascades such as Wnt/beta-catenin and receptor tyrosine kinase pathways drive growth factor independence and resistance to growth inhibition.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how malignant cells fail to undergo terminal lineage differentiation using examples from hematopoiesis and colonic crypt epithelium.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis, replicative immortality, and p53 stress surveillance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how cancer cells overcome intrinsic limits to survival and division through apoptotic resistance, telomere maintenance, and the bypass of p53-mediated senescence.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine alterations in cancer cell metabolism, including aerobic glycolysis and Krebs cycle mutations that produce driver oncometabolites.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis and the angiogenic switch
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the requirement of growing tumors to induce new blood vessel formation to supply oxygen and nutrients.

topics.label: Mechanisms, dissemination, and genetics of cancer metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the progression of metastasis from local invasion and vascular dissemination to colonization inefficiency and genomic features.

topics.label: Lecture summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer reviews the core concepts covered in the session and provides final concluding remarks.
